author: rodriguescarson
body:
Thanks for picking this up. That's the exact case from #1776, same store, and the warning text names the two things I was missing at the time: that the store is single-scale, and that `vc_gen_normalgrids pyramid` can derive the levels from a local copy. I'd assumed the multiscale grids had to be published; they don't.

I've added the pyramid route to the params write-up I keep for `vc_grow_seg_from_seed`, pointing here, so anyone who hits the slow level-0 run has the fix in one place.

author: nerln
body:
Independent reproduction, before and after, same surface: on the official PHerc1218 single-scale normal-grid store, `normal_grid_level=2` is silently dropped to level 0 on upstream main (4b3c72882, this branch's base) and produces the new warning on this branch (c48953d86), with the generated surface unchanged (400.716970 vx^2 in all four runs). Both binaries built on macOS arm64.

Setup: the official store `20250521120456-surface-20260413222639-surface-m7-L0-th0.2.normal-grids`, streamed through a `normal-grids-remote.json` marker, and its surface-prediction zarr. Seed 3328 3390 11584, 1 generation, no `step_size` in params (the grid's own spiral step, 20, is picked up automatically). Command: `vc_grow_seg_from_seed -v <volume> -t <out> -p <params.json> -s 3328 3390 11584`.

Before, `normal_grid_level=2`: exit 0, 32 s, 46 MiB of grid files fetched; log reads `Loaded normal grid level 0 (coordinate_scale=1, output_spiral_step=20)`, no warning. This store's `metadata.json` has no `"format"` key, so the multiscale check is false and it falls back to level 0 without a word: the single-scale case this PR addresses.

Before, `normal_grid_level=7` (clamped to 5 by `GrowPatch.cpp`'s own `std::clamp(..., 0, 5)` before it reaches `NormalGridVolume`): exit 0, 20 s, same `Loaded normal grid level 0` line, again no warning.

After, `normal_grid_level=2`: exit 0, 16 s, same surface; log now reads `warning: normal_grid_level=2 ignored; store at <store> is single-scale (no "format":"normal-grid-multiscale" in metadata.json); using level 0. A multiscale store can be derived from a local copy with vc_gen_normalgrids pyramid -i <store> -o <multiscale store>`, printed immediately before the same `Loaded normal grid level 0` line. After, `normal_grid_level=7`: same warning with `normal_grid_level=5`, same surface. So the fix adds exactly the expected warning, on the requested level and on the GrowPatch-clamped one, without changing the output.

Not exercised: the multiscale "outside the levels X..Y" branch, which needs a multiscale store (`vc_gen_normalgrids pyramid`); the official store is single-scale.

Two notes from the diff, not from running anything, and not asking to expand the PR: the single-scale warning keys on `"format" == "normal-grid-multiscale"`, so a hand-built multiscale store missing that key would still be reported as single-scale; and the new doctests capture stderr only around the constructor, so a `base_path` with a symlink or trailing slash is not covered as far as the printed path goes.

author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Thanks @nerln for reproducing this on the official PHerc1218 store, both the requested level and the GrowPatch-clamped one, with the surface unchanged.

On the two notes:

- The `"format": "normal-grid-multiscale"` check is the existing detection in `NormalGridVolume`; this PR only adds the warnings around it. `vc_gen_normalgrids pyramid` writes that key, so a hand-built multiscale store without it was already treated as single-scale before this change, and now says so instead of staying silent.
- The doctests capture `std::cerr` only around the constructor because that is the only place the warnings are emitted. The path in the message is `base_path` exactly as passed (symlink or trailing slash included), the same way the other messages in that class print it.

Not expanding the PR for either; both are notes worth having on record.

AI-assisted (Claude Code), human-directed.
